headline: A 31% volume increase over four weeks has landed cleanly, with easy-run heart rate dropping meaningfully at comparable efforts — aerobic adaptation is tracking in the right direction.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The recent block represents a genuine step up in load, not just on paper but with a physiological signal to match: your easy-run HR has come down noticeably against the prior period at similar efforts and paces. That kind of drift — more work, lower cardiac cost — is the clearest within-athlete marker that the volume is being absorbed rather than merely tolerated.

Today's run sits comfortably in the aerobic development zone: flat terrain, controlled HR, solid distance. Coming two days after the July 2nd effort, the back-to-back pattern is relevant context — you're building durability as much as raw fitness, and the HR response across consecutive days suggests recovery capacity is holding up well under the increased load.

The 20-week running streak matching your personal best is worth naming, not as a milestone to protect at all costs, but because unbroken consistency at this volume level — combined with six strength sessions in each of the last two four-week blocks — is what underpins the kind of aerobic adaptation you're currently seeing. The foundation is genuinely solid.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR continues to trend down or plateaus as load stays elevated — a plateau is normal and expected; a reversal would be worth noting.
Monitor how consecutive-day running efforts feel subjectively, particularly leg heaviness and pace feel at controlled HR — this will tell you more than the numbers alone about durability progress.
Keep an eye on whether strength quality is maintained as running volume holds at this higher level — session quality matters more than session count here.
The lactate threshold data point is very recent and isolated — watch for a second test opportunity to start building a meaningful trend line.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 163 km vs 125 km prior block (+31%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 6 runs)
